evidence: FACT (tier-1-adjacent, Q3 FY2026 results released 2026-09-02, post-dating the supplied filings): Q3 revenue $29.6B; AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B, +221% YoY and +54% QoQ. Q4 guidance: AI semiconductor revenue $21.7B (+236% YoY) and consolidated revenue $34.8B (+93% YoY). Combining actuals and guidance gives FY2026 revenue near $105.9B, +65.8% on FY2025.

INFERENCE: custom AI silicon (XPU) is the hyperscalers' STRUCTURAL HEDGE against merchant GPU pricing. Broadcom therefore participates in the AI build-out on a different axis from NVDA rather than as a correlated proxy — it wins when customers want to escape merchant economics.
FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Two engines, not one: semiconductor solutions $36,858M and infrastructure software $27,029M of FY2025 revenue (58%/42%).
counter_evidence: INFERENCE: Broadcom largely EXECUTES customer architectures rather than defining them. The IP direction on an XPU comes substantially from the customer, which is why this scores 13 rather than the 14 assigned to NVDA and TSM.

FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Infrastructure software growth has decelerated sharply — +26% in FY2025 but only +5.1% in H1 FY2026 and +8.8% in Q2. The VMware subscription conversion is largely complete, so the second engine is now close to ex-growth.
The stock fell about 6.5% after hours on the Q3 print despite a 221% AI revenue increase, on a Q4 outlook below some expectations — the market is already discounting a high growth path.

evidence: FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Semiconductor solutions operating margin expanded from 55.7% (FY2024) to 57.6% (FY2025) to 61.8% in Q2 FY2026 — customers are paying more, not less, as volume scales.

FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Infrastructure software operating margin of 76.8% in FY2025 and 78.7% in Q2 FY2026 is exceptional and demonstrates real pricing power over an installed base.
INFERENCE: once an XPU design is won, switching costs are very high for the life of that program — the customer has co-invested engineering years into the silicon.
counter_evidence: FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Customer value is concentrated in very few relationships. Distributors overall were 56% of revenue, from 48% in FY2025.
INFERENCE: XPU sockets are RE-COMPETED at each generation, unlike a platform with an installed software ecosystem. Marvell, MediaTek and Alchip compete for the same designs.

INFERENCE: the VMware repricing that produced the software margin also produced customer resentment; a 78.7% margin on infrastructure software invites both substitution effort and regulatory attention.

evidence: FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Semiconductor margin expanding 55.7% to 61.8% while segment revenue grew 78.5% YoY in Q2 FY2026 is genuine positive direction.
FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): R&D $5,253M (FY2023) to $9,310M (FY2024) to $10,977M (FY2025), 17% of revenue — sustained investment in the XPU and networking franchises.

evidence: FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): THE MOST ASSET-LIGHT BUSINESS IN THIS HARNESS: FY2025 capex of $623M on $63,887M of revenue — 1.0%. FY2024 $548M, FY2023 $452M.

counter_evidence: FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): THE PER-SHARE TEST FAILS. evidence: FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): THE VMWARE ACQUISITION IS WORKING ON ITS OWN TERMS: infrastructure software delivered $20,765M of FY2025 operating income on 42% of revenue at a 76.8% margin, versus $13,977M the prior year (+49%).

FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Deleveraging while returning capital: total debt principal reduced from $69,847M (FY2024) to $67,120M (FY2025) to $66,720M (Q2 FY2026) while paying $11,142M of FY2025 dividends.
INFERENCE: the serial-acquirer playbook — buy, reprice, cut cost, harvest — has been executed repeatedly and demonstrably creates accounting profit.
counter_evidence: FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): THE BALANCE SHEET IS GOODWILL. Goodwill of $97,801M plus intangibles of $32,273M equals $130,074M of the $171,092M total asset base — 76%. Total stockholders' equity is $81,292M, so GOODWILL ALONE EXCEEDS BOOK EQUITY BY ROUGHLY $16.5B and tangible book value is deeply negative.

FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): FY2025 net income of $23,126M EXCEEDS pretax income of $22,729M because of a $397M tax BENEFIT, against a $3,748M provision the prior year. An unexplained swing of this size in the headline earnings line warrants investigation.

FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Acquisition-related intangible amortisation was $8,062M in FY2025 ($6,031M in cost of revenue plus $2,031M in operating expense) — 32% of reported operating income. Combined with SBC, the GAAP-to-non-GAAP margin gap is roughly 20 percentage points.

FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Debt is being reduced rather than grown: $69,847M to $67,120M to $66,720M principal across FY2024, FY2025 and Q2 FY2026.
counter_evidence: FACT (tier-1, 10-K FY2025 / 10-Q Q2 FY2026): Net debt of approximately $47.1B is real leverage, incurred for VMware, and is the highest in this harness — Samsung, NVDA and TSM all hold net cash.

This scores 8 rather than the 9 assigned to the other three names for exactly these two reasons.

evidence: At $357.16 (2026-09-03 close) and 4,758M shares, market capitalisation is approximately $1,699B; adding net debt of about $47.1B gives an enterprise value near $1,747B.

evidence: Permanent-loss risk is low in the ordinary sense: operating cash flow of $27.5B against $2.7B of cash interest leaves no plausible insolvency path.
The bull case is specific: if XPU becomes the dominant AI compute paradigm across multiple hyperscaler programmes, FY2031 revenue of $300-350B is reachable from a $106B base.
counter_evidence: STRUCTURAL CAP: at roughly $1.70T a 10x outcome implies a $17T company. Modelled bull upside is +63% to +90%.

THE BEAR IS AMPLIFIED BY TWO THINGS THE OTHER NAMES LACK: leverage of about $47.1B net debt, and a 42% single-customer dependence. Losing or halving that one relationship is not a margin event, it is a business-model event. Modelled bear is -70% to -55%.
This scores 4 rather than 5 because the downside is levered and concentration-driven while the upside is capped — a worse outcome shape than NVDA's.
